title: UPSC Daily Current Affairs MCQs Master List
subject: Current Affairs

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA) rules, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: The Jharkhand Cabinet approved the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA) rules, empowering Gram Sabhas with wider administrative and decision-making powers in Fifth Schedule areas.Statement 1 is correct:PESA is intended to recognise, empower, and promote the Scheduled Tribes’ social, economic, cultural, and political traditions.Statement 2 is not correct:It also directs thestate government(not District Magistrate) to delegate powers and authority to Gram Sabha and Panchayats.Statement 3 is not correct:The majority of the North Eastern states in Sixth Schedule Areas (where autonomous councils exist) arenot covered by PESAbecause they have their own autonomous councils for governance.

questions.question_text: Q2. With reference to the United Nations Assistance Mission, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:UN Assistance Missions are established by the Security Council to assist countries with peacebuilding, political dialogue, etc.Statement 2 is correct:UNAMA (Afghanistan) was founded in 2002.Statement 3 is not correct:UNAMI (Iraq) has been instrumental in providing electoral aid to Iraq, assisting with the implementation of many rounds of municipal and national elections.

questions.question_text: Q3. With reference to the Development of Solar Parks and Ultra-Mega Solar Power Projects scheme, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:The scheme encourages states/UTs to prioritise government-owned waste or non-agricultural land for setting up solar parks.Statement 2 is not correct:Launched in 2014 (not 2018), the scheme has approved 55 parks.Statement 3 is not correct:The capacity of the solar parks shall be 500 MW and above (not 1000 MW).Statement 4 is correct:These parks are proposed to be set up by 2025-26.

questions.question_text: Q4. The principles of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) refer to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: The responsibilities of nations to fight climate change in proportion to their historic contributions in emitting planet-warming greenhouse gases.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Equal climate obligations for all countries regardless of development status.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Voluntary climate action determined solely by national economic growth rates.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Responsibility of only developed countries to address environmental degradation.

questions.explanation: India approaches UNEA-7 with the conviction that global action must be guided by the principles of equity, Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC). The principles of CBDR-RC refer to the responsibilities of nations to fight climate change in proportion to their historic contributions in emitting planet-warming greenhouse gases.

questions.question_text: Q5. With reference to the MH 60R helicopter, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:The Indian Navy commissioned its second MH 60R helicopter squadron, INAS 335, at INS Hansa in Goa.Statement 2 is correct:It can be used for vertical replenishment (VERTREP).Statement 3 is correct:These helicopters are replacing the ageing British-origin Sea King helicopters.Statement 4 is not correct:These US-origin Seahawks (Black Hawk maritime version) are imported, not manufactured by HAL.

questions.question_text: Q1. Who among the following were not members of the 1946 Cabinet Mission to India, which consisted of three senior British Cabinet ministers?
questions.explanation: By the 1940s, especially after World War II ended and Winston Churchill lost power, the withdrawal of the British from India was seen as more or less inevitable.On March 24, 1946, three British Cabinet ministers under Prime Minister Clement Attlee were sent to India. The three were Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Secretary of State for India; Sir Stafford Cripps, President of the Board of Trade; and A V Alexander, First Lord of the Admiralty.The Viceroy of India was then Lord Archibald Wavell(not a member of the mission).

questions.question_text: Q2. Consider the following statements regarding National Awards:
questions.explanation: The Bombay High Court while pointing to the manner in which a plea’s case title was written said that civilian awards such as “Padma Shri” and “Bharat Ratna” are not titles and cannot be used as prefix or suffix to names of the awardees.Statement 2 is correct:The high court referred to a five-judge Constitution bench decision of the apex court which had held that civilian awards such as Padma Shri and Bharat Ratna are not titles and ought not to be used as prefix or suffix to names of the awardees.Statement 1 is not correct:The Supreme Court in Balaji Raghavan/SP Anand v. Union of India had answered whether the awards, Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri are “Titles” within the meaning of Article 18(1) (abolition of titles) of the Constitution. The National Awards do not amount to “titles” within the meaning of Article 18(1) and they should not be used as suffixes or prefixes.

questions.question_text: Q3. India pledged to provide $450 million in humanitarian aid for the reconstruction in the wake of destruction caused by Cyclone Ditwah for which country?
questions.explanation: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar pledged $450 million in humanitarian aid toSri Lankato deal with the aftermath of Cyclone Ditwah. This is part of India’s First Responder activity under Operation Sagar Bandhu.

questions.question_text: Q4. Which of the following is/are required for carry trade?
questions.explanation: A carry trade involves borrowing at a low interest rate and investing in an asset with a higher rate of return.Carry trades thrive under two conditions: a significantinterest rate differentialandcurrency stability. It is most recognised for its application in foreign exchange (forex or FX) markets.

questions.question_text: Q5. With reference to the Octopuses, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:Octopuses are soft-bodied molluscs that usually crawl along the seafloor instead of swimming long distances.Statement 2 is correct:Two of their hearts (branchial hearts) pump blood directly to the gills, where oxygen is absorbed.Statement 3 is not correct:Octopuses havethreehearts, not four (two branchial and one systemic).Statement 4 is correct:When an octopus swims, it uses jet propulsion by quickly pushing water out through a siphon.

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the H3 rocket, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:Japan’s space mission onboard the H3 rocket suffered failure at the second stage after lift-off. It is the H3-24L from the same H3 series of heavy life-off rockets which will launch the Chandrayaan-5 planned sometime in 2028-2029.Statement 2 is correct:Also known as Lunar Polar Exploration (LUPEX), the Chandrayaan-5 mission is being jointly developed by ISRO and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). It will study the volatile materials, lunar water in the vicinity of a Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR) in the lunar south pole. Chandrayaan-5 will carry an ISRO-made lunar lander and the rover is being developed by Japan.

questions.question_text: Q2. Consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:Gopinath Bordoloi (also spelt Bardoloi), the CM of Assam, was against the lumping together of Assam with Bengal. The Assam Provincial Congress Committee totally rejected this grouping in the plan. The leaders of the Assam Provincial Congress feared that under this ‘grouping’ Assam might be sacrificed and tagged to Muslim dominated zone to appease the League.Statement 2 is correct:Nehru felt that the Cabinet Mission Plan had been devised because the British wanted to “save the face of Jinnah” and not push him into an “impossible corner”. He opposed Assam being forced into anything.

questions.question_text: Q3. With reference to the personality rights, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: The Delhi High Court restrained the unauthorised commercial use of actor R Madhavan’s image and likeness, ordered the takedown of obscene and AI-generated material circulating online.Statement 2 is correct:Personality Rights safeguard an individual’s name, image, likeness, voice, signature and other identifiable traits from unauthorised commercial exploitation.Statement 1 is not correct:India does not have a standalone statute defining these rights. Instead, courts have assembled them through a combination of intellectual property law and constitutional principles.Statement 3 is correct:Section 38A of the Copyright Act grants performers exclusive rights, once consent is provided for commercial use of their performances. Section 38B recognises the moral rights of performers. There is no provision in the Constitution of India about the moral rights.

questions.question_text: Q4. India has signed a collaboration agreement with which country for the transfer of the SIGMA 30N Digital Ring Laser Gyro Inertial Navigation System?
questions.explanation: The state-owned India Optel Limited (IOL) signed a collaboration agreement withFrance’sSafran Electronics and Defense for the transfer of production of two high-precision, combat-proven systems—the SIGMA 30N Digital Ring Laser Gyro Inertial Navigation System, used in artillery guns, air defence systems, missiles and radars, and the CM3-MR Direct Firing Sight.

questions.question_text: Q5. Open Market Operations (OMOs) are the market operations conducted by the RBI in which:

options.label: A
options.option_text: It sells/purchases securities to/from the market to adjust the rupee liquidity conditions.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It fixes the repo and reverse repo rates to influence short-term interest rates.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It directly lends funds to commercial banks against collateral for overnight needs.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It regulates foreign exchange rates by buying and selling foreign currencies in the spot market.

questions.explanation: OMOs are the market operations conducted by the RBI by way ofsale/ purchase of G-Secs to/ from the marketwith an objective to adjust the rupee liquidity conditions in the market on a durable basis. When the RBI feels that there is excess liquidity in the market, it resorts to sale of securities thereby sucking out the rupee liquidity. Similarly, when the liquidity conditions are tight, RBI may buy securities from the market, thereby releasing liquidity into the market.

questions.question_text: Q1. The Rajmachi Trek, Chembra Peak, and Tadiandamol Trek are located on the:
questions.explanation: These treks are located in theWestern Ghats.Rajmachi Trekis situated in the Sahyadri range of the Western Ghats (Maharashtra).Chembra Peakis located near Wayanad (Kerala), an excellent introduction to trekking in the southern Western Ghats.Tadiandamolis the highest peak in Coorg (Karnataka).

questions.question_text: Q2. Data exclusivity is a regulatory protection in:
questions.explanation: Data exclusivity is a regulatory protection inPharmaceuticals. This provision grants innovator pharmaceutical companies exclusive rights over the clinical trial data submitted to regulators, preventing them from using this data to approve generic versions for a specific period.

questions.question_text: Q3. “It must be kept out of unhealthy competition with political parties and communal bodies. For these and other similar reasons, the A.I.C.C. (All India Congress Committee) resolves to disband the existing Congress organisation and flower into a Lok Sevak Sangh (Society to Serve the People).”Who wrote the above words about Congress?
questions.explanation: By the 1940s,Mahatma Gandhibelieved that decentralised action to achieve self-rule was the best path. Shortly before his assassination in 1948, he wrote about the Congress, “It must be kept out of unhealthy competition... the A.I.C.C. resolves to disband the existing Congress organisation and flower into a Lok Sevak Sangh.”

questions.question_text: Q4. With reference to the following cases, consider the following pairs:
questions.explanation: Since the mid-1990s, the Supreme Court has relied on two long-running public interest cases to regulate environmental governance.Pair 1 is correct:T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v Union of India (1995) redefined "forest" and regulated non-forest activities like mining.Pair 2 is correct:M.C. questions.question_text: Q5. Israel became the first United Nations (UN) member state to officially recognise the Republic of Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state. The Republic of Somaliland is located in:
questions.explanation: Somaliland is a self-declared republic in theHorn of Africa. Israel became the first UN member state to officially recognise it. It declared independence from Somalia in 1991 and has remained de-facto independent, though internationally recognised as part of Somalia.

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the trade between India and New Zealand, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: India and New Zealand announced the conclusion of negotiations on a free trade agreement.Statement 2 is correct:The FTA sets the stage for doubling bilateral trade in the coming 5 years.Statement 1 is not correct:The trade did not rise every single year — it dipped in 2023-24 compared to 2022-23 and then increased in 2024-25.Statement 3 is not correct:Recent data show India has had a trade surplus with New Zealand in merchandise trade in recent years.

questions.question_text: Q2. The Al Maszhabiya region is a:
questions.explanation: The Al Maszhabiya region is adesert in southwestern Qatar. It is a 21-million-year-old bonebed, filled with the remains of sea cows, sharks, barracuda-like fish, prehistoric dolphins, and sea turtles. Recently, a new species of sea cow,Salwasiren qatarensis, was discovered here.

questions.question_text: Q3. Which of the following launching vehicles was used to launch the communication satellite BlueBird Block-2?
questions.explanation: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) launched theLVM-3 rocketcarrying its heaviest-ever satellite — BlueBird Block-2, weighing nearly 6,100 kg. This mission marks the third time the LVM-3 will be used to carry a satellite into Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

questions.question_text: Q4. “The British government in India has not only deprived the Indian people of their freedom but has based itself on the exploitation of the masses, and has ruined India economically, politically, culturally and spiritually… Therefore… India must sever the British connection and attain Purna Swaraj or complete independence.”Whose words are these?
questions.explanation: At the 1929 Lahore session of the Congress, under the presidency of Gandhi’s protegeJawaharlal Nehru, the party declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as its ultimate goal. Nehru declared, “The British government in India has not only deprived the Indian people of their freedom... Therefore... India must sever the British connection and attain Purna Swaraj or complete independence.”

questions.question_text: Q5. With reference to the Language to be used in Parliament, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Article 120 of the Constitution of India provides for the language to be used in Parliament.Statement 1 is not correct:Notwithstanding anything in Part XVII, but subject to the provisions of article 348, business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or in English.Statement 2 is not correct:Provided that theChairman of the Council of States or Speaker of the House of the People(not the Chairman of the Business Advisory Committee), or person acting as such, may permit any member who cannot adequately express himself in Hindi or in English to address the House in his mother-tongue.

questions.question_text: Q1. Which of the following countries is holding its first phase of election under military rule in 5 years?
questions.explanation: Voters inMyanmarwent to the polls for the first phase of the country’s first general election in five years, held under the control of the military government. Voting took place at schools, government offices and religious buildings in Yangon, Naypyitaw and other locations.

questions.question_text: Q2. Which of the following banks are required to maintain a Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)?
questions.explanation: All are required.As per Section 24 (2A) of the Banking Regulation Act 1949, Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks shall maintain liquid assets (SLR).As per Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act 1949, State Co-operative Banks (SCBs) and District Central Co-operative Banks (DCCBs) are also required to maintain assets as part of the SLR requirement.

questions.question_text: Q5. “I am sending thither Abdullah my ambassador and Dominic Pires to ask you to send me two learned Priests, who should bring with them the Principal books of the Law and the Gospel so that I may leam the Law and what is most perfect in it.”Which Mughal emperor’s invitation (above) surprised the Jesuits, who saw it as a chance to convert the Muslim rulers of the north to Christianity?
questions.explanation: About five centuries back, the Mughal emperorAkbarsent out a request to Jesuit priests stationed at the Portuguese enclave of Goa to teach him about Christianity. His invitation came as a big surprise to the Jesuits who saw in it an opportunity to teach the laws of Christianity to the Muslim rulers of north.

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the electoral trusts, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: With the scrapping of the electoral bonds scheme, companies have again turned to electoral trusts as a preferred source of political donations.Statement 2 is correct:While the electoral bonds scheme sought to ensure donor anonymity, electoral trusts are required to report to the Election Commission contributions from individuals and companies, and their donations to parties every year.Statement 1 is correct:Under Section 17CA of the Income Tax Act of 1961, any citizen of India, a company registered in India, or a firm or Hindu Undivided Family or association of persons living in India, can donate to an electoral trust.Statement 3 is not correct:Electoral trusts must apply for renewal everythreefinancial years.Statement 4 is not correct:They must donate95%of contributions received in a financial year to political parties registered under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

questions.question_text: Q2. Consider the following statements about the Global Environment Facility (GEF):
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:The GEF was formed on the eve of the 1992 Rio Earth Summit.Statement 2 is correct:It is a financial mechanism for five major international environmental conventions, including the Minamata Convention on Mercury.Statement 3 is not correct:GEF is a partnership between 18 institutions, including UNDP, UNEP, the World Bank, and FAO, not exclusively UNEP.Statement 4 is not correct:GEF provides funding primarily todeveloping countriesand economies in transition, not only to developed countries.

questions.question_text: Q1. Consider the following statements with the reference to Vande Mataram, the song written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay:

questions.question_text: Q2. Consider the following:“A member of the legislature is disqualified if convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than two years. The only relief in such cases is a stay of the conviction, which would immediately void its consequences, such as disqualification.”The above statement is provided under:
questions.explanation: As per theRepresentation of the People Act, 1951, a member of the legislature is disqualified if convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than two years. The only relief in such cases is a stay of the conviction.

questions.question_text: Q3. Which of the following countries has faced near-zero real economic growth — averaging around 0.4 per cent between 1999-2000 and 2023-24 — along with persistently low inflation?
questions.explanation: For over two decades,Japanhas faced near-zero real economic growth — averaging around 0.4% between 1999-2000 and 2023-24 — along with persistently low inflation. One of the major challenges for the economy has been an unfavourable demographic shift (rapid ageing).

questions.question_text: Q2. Which of the following statements is/are correct with reference to ‘Kalaka Acharya Katha’?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It tells the tale of a Jain monk who seeks help from the Sakas.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is a Buddhist text belonging to the Tripitaka.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It was originally written in Sanskrit and only later adapted into Prakrit.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The text describes the construction of ancient Hindu temples in western India.

Many manuscripts also included appendices such as theKalaka Acharya Katha, recounting how the sage Kalaka invited foreign kings, especially Sakas, to punish an arrogant ruler of Ujjain who had abducted his sister.

questions.question_text: Q5. Recently, the Deir ez-Zor and Raqqa provinces were in the news due to the US military strike. These provinces are located in:

questions.question_text: Q1. The ‘Project Suncatcher’ is related to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: A global initiative to mine rare-earth minerals from the Moon for renewable energy technologies.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It will equip solar-powered satellite constellations with Tensor Processing Units.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A defence project aimed at deploying space-based laser systems for missile interception.

options.label: D
options.option_text: An ISRO–NASA collaboration for wireless power transmission from space-based nuclear reactors.

Project Suncatcher willequip solar-powered satellite constellations with Tensor Processing Units(Google’s patented chip capable of high-volume, low-precision computation) and optical links that may scale machine learning computations in space.

questions.question_text: Q2. The “Adjournment Motion” refers to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: A motion introduced to regulate the conduct of business of the House

options.label: B
options.option_text: A motion moved to express regret over the death of a sitting member of Parliament

options.label: C
options.option_text: A Motion for discussing a specific and important matter that should have urgent consideration

options.label: D
options.option_text: A motion related to the consideration and passing of a Money Bill

questions.explanation: Adjournment Motion is a motion fordiscussing ‘a specific and important matter that should have urgent consideration’. It can be moved by any member of the House and is in the nature of an emergency motion of censure upon the Government. The object is to draw the attention of the Government to a matter of urgent public importance.

questions.question_text: Q3. With reference to the Reciprocal Exchange of Logistics Support (RELOS), consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: The Reciprocal Exchange of Logistics Support (RELOS) was ratified by both houses of the Russian Parliament before receiving presidential approval.Statement 2 is correct:It has been signed between India and Russia.Statements 1 and 3 are correct:The agreement sets out procedures governing the movement of military formations, warships, and military aircraft, and it will facilitate the mutual use of airspace by Russian and Indian military aircraft.

questions.question_text: Q4. Consider the following excerpt:“There is no question of some Muslims objecting to Vande Mataram. That has not influenced many people here, but many of us, and I feel strongly about it, think that in the present context Vande Mataram is completely unsuited as a national anthem... A national anthem should be something of victory and fulfilment, not of past struggle.”Whose words are these?
questions.explanation: In a Cabinet note on May 21, 1948,Jawaharlal Nehruspelled out his reasons for choosing Jana Gana Mana over Vande Mataram as the national anthem. He wrote to Congress leader B C Roy saying that a national anthem should be something of victory and fulfilment, not of past struggle.

questions.question_text: Q5. With reference to the Shyok Tunnel, consider the following statements:

questions.question_text: Q1. Who among the following was known as ‘Father of Indian Modern Dance’?
questions.explanation: Uday Shankar(1900-1977) was a pioneering Indian dancer and choreographer. He created a new fusion style of dance by blending traditional Indian classical, folk, and tribal forms with Western theatrical techniques. He is considered the father of modern Indian dance for his innovative approach, which gained international recognition and broke the taboo surrounding dance in society at the time.

questions.question_text: Q2. With reference to Assisted dying, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct:Assisted dying is an intention to cause death through the administration of a lethal injection. In India, this directly attracts criminal liability.Statement 1 is correct:Assisted dying is treated as murder under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), or at the minimum, as culpable homicide. When a doctor assists the patient in performing the act, criminal liability arises for abetment to suicide.

questions.question_text: Q3. With reference to the deposit insurance, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: The DICGC aims to safeguard “small depositors” from the risk of losing their savings.Statement 1 is correct:The insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh per depositor applies to all accounts held by the depositor at all branches of the insured bank.Statement 2 is not correct:The DICGC insures all commercial banks (including foreign bank branches, local area banks, RRBs, and cooperative banks), but itdoes not cover primary cooperative societies.

questions.question_text: Q4. With reference to the sea cows, consider the following statements:

questions.question_text: Q5. The World Health Organisation, in its 2001 guidance on uranium in drinking water, said that the human body, on average, contains about 90 µg of uranium. What is the correct order of uranium content (from low to high) in the human body?1. Liver2. Kidney3. Skeleton
questions.explanation: According to the WHO (2001), the distribution of uranium in the human body is:- Skeleton: ~66%- Liver: ~16%- Kidney: ~8%- Other tissues: ~10%The correct order from low to high isKidney (8%) -> Liver (16%) -> Skeleton (66%). Thus, 2—1—3.

questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct:NALSA is constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 to provide free Legal Services to weaker sections and organize Lok Adalats.Statement 3 is not correct:The Chief Justice of India serves as thePatron-in-Chief. The Executive Chairman is a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge selected by the Chief Justice of India.

Currently, Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) and Loktak Lake (Manipur) are the two Indian sites on the record.

questions.question_text: Q5. With reference to 'Web 3.0', consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:Web 3.0 refers to the next generation of the internet, characterized by decentralization, where applications run on blockchains or decentralized peer-to-peer networks.Statement 2 is correct:A key feature of Web 3.0 is user sovereignty, enabling users to own their data and digital assets (like NFTs) via blockchain.Statement 3 is not correct:Unlike Web 2.0, which relies on centralized servers (Google, Amazon, etc.), Web 3.0 aims to reduce dependency on central authorities.

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA), consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:PESA extends the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution to the Scheduled Areas of the Fifth Schedule.Statement 2 is correct:The Act empowers the Gram Sabha with the ownership of minor forest produce.Statement 3 is correct:The recommendation of the Gram Sabha is mandatory for granting prospecting licenses or mining leases forminor minerals(not all minerals) in the Scheduled Areas.

questions.question_text: Q2. Which of the following foreign travelers visited the Vijayanagara Empire during the reign of Deva Raya II?
questions.explanation: Abdur Razzak, the Persian ambassador sent by Shah Rukh (timurid dynasty), visited the Vijayanagara Empire during the reign ofDeva Raya II(Sangama Dynasty).Nicolo Conti visited during Deva Raya I.Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz visited during the Tuluva dynasty rule (Krishnadevaraya and Achyuta Raya respectively).

questions.question_text: Q3. With reference to ‘Participatory Notes’ (P-Notes), consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:Participatory Notes (P-Notes) are issued by registered Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to overseas investors who wish to invest in the Indian stock market without registering themselves directly.Statement 2 is not correct:The primary purpose of P-Notes is to allow investors to investwithoutregistering directly with SEBI, although they are subject to KYC norms.

questions.question_text: Q4. With reference to the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:The 2022 rules expanded the definition of e-waste to explicitly include solar photo-voltaic modules/panels/cells.Statement 2 is correct:The rules reinforce the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework, making producers responsible for the collection and recycling of e-waste.

questions.question_text: Q5. In the context of quantum computing, what is a ‘Qubit’?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A unit of data that can exist in a state of 0, 1, or both simultaneously

options.label: B
options.option_text: A new type of silicon chip used for faster processing in classical computers

options.label: C
options.option_text: A unit of energy required to cool a supercomputer

options.label: D
options.option_text: A protocol for secure internet communication

questions.explanation: AQubit(Quantum Bit) is the basic unit of information in quantum computing. Unlike a classical bit, which can be either 0 or 1, a qubit can exist in a state of superposition, representing both 0 and 1 simultaneously [attachment_0](attachment), allowing quantum computers to solve certain problems exponentially faster.

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the Attorney General of India (AGI), consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:The AGI is appointed by the President of India under Article 76.Statement 2 is not correct:The Constitution does not fix the remuneration of the AGI. He receives such remuneration as the President may determine.Statement 3 is correct:In the performance of his official duties, the Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.

questions.question_text: Q2. The Ilbert Bill controversy during the viceroyalty of Lord Ripon related to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Imposition of restrictions on the vernacular press

options.label: B
options.option_text: Removal of disqualifications imposed on the Indian magistrates with regard to the trial of the Europeans

options.label: C
options.option_text: Imposition of additional duty on imports of cotton from Manchester

options.label: D
options.option_text: Restrictions on the entry of Indians into the Indian Civil Service

questions.explanation: TheIlbert Bill (1883)sought to allow senior Indian magistrates to preside over cases involving British subjects in India. The bill caused widespread anger among the British community in India (the White Mutiny), forcing the government to withdraw the bill and introduce a compromised version.

questions.question_text: Q3. In the context of the banking sector, the term 'Capital Adequacy Ratio' (CAR) is defined as:

options.label: A
options.option_text: The ratio of a bank's total deposits to its total loans

options.label: B
options.option_text: The ratio of a bank's capital to its risk-weighted assets

options.label: C
options.option_text: The percentage of total deposits that a bank must keep with the RBI in cash

options.label: D
options.option_text: The profit earned by a bank on its total assets

questions.explanation: Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), also known as Capital to Risk (Weighted) Assets Ratio (CRAR), is the ratio of a bank's capital to its risk. It ensures that the bank has enough cushion to absorb a reasonable amount of losses and protects depositors.

questions.question_text: Q4. With reference to Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus), consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is not correct:Red Sanders is endemic to a distinct tract of forests in theEastern Ghatsregion of Andhra Pradesh, not the Western Ghats.Statement 2 is correct:It is listed inAppendix IIof CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora), which means trade must be controlled to avoid utilization incompatible with their survival.

questions.question_text: Q5. The 'Kármán line' is an attempt to define a boundary between:
questions.explanation: TheKármán lineis an attempt to define a boundary betweenEarth's atmosphere and outer space. The Fédération Aéronautique Internationale (FAI) defines the Kármán line as the altitude of 100 kilometres (62 miles) above Earth's mean sea level.

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the Ordinance-making power of the President of India, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is not correct:The President can promulgate an ordinance wheneitherof the two Houses of Parliament is not in session (or both are not in session). An ordinance can be issued even if one House is in session because a law cannot be passed by one House alone.Statement 2 is correct:An ordinance must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of its reassembly. Since the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot exceed six months, the maximum life of an ordinance is six months and six weeks.

questions.question_text: Q3. The term ‘Angel Tax’, often seen in the news, is levied on:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Profits made by foreign institutional investors in the stock market

options.label: B
options.option_text: Capital raised by unlisted companies from investors above the fair market value of shares

options.option_text: Digital services provided by foreign tech giants

questions.explanation: Angel Taxrefers to the income tax payable on capital raised by unlisted companies (like startups) via the issue of shares where the share price is seen in excess of the fair market value of the shares sold. It is treated as 'income from other sources'.

questions.question_text: Q4. The ‘MISHTI’ scheme, announced in the Union Budget, focuses on:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Providing nutritional support to pregnant women

options.label: B
options.option_text: Mangrove plantation along the coastline and on salt pan lands

questions.question_text: Q5. With reference to the Aditya-L1 mission, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:Aditya-L1 is the first Indian space-based observatory-class solar mission to study the Sun.Statement 2 is correct:The spacecraft is placed in a halo orbit around the Lagrange point 1 (L1) of the Sun-Earth system, which is about 1.5 million km from the Earth. A satellite placed in the halo orbit around the L1 point has the major advantage of continuously viewing the Sun without any occultation/eclipses.

questions.question_text: Q1. The ‘Sarkaria Commission’ was appointed in 1983 to examine and review:
questions.explanation: TheSarkaria Commissionwas set up in 1983 by the central government of India to examine the relationship and balance of power between state and central governments (Centre-State relations). Its report is a cornerstone in Indian federalism.

questions.question_text: Q2. With reference to the Ghadar Party, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct.The Ghadar Party was an international political movement founded by expatriate Indians to overthrow British rule in India. It was headquartered in San Francisco (at the Yugantar Ashram) and founded in 1913. Key leaders included Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna. Their newspaper 'The Ghadar' carried the caption 'Angrezi Raj Ka Dushman' (Enemy of British Rule).

questions.question_text: Q3. In the context of the banking sector, ‘Capital Adequacy Ratio’ (CAR) is essentially:

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.option_text: The ratio of a bank's capital to its risk-weighted assets

options.option_text: The ratio of a bank's non-performing assets to its total assets

options.label: D
options.option_text: The percentage of loans given to the priority sector

questions.question_text: Q4. The ‘Bonn Convention’ is related to the conservation of:
questions.explanation: TheConvention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS), also known as theBonn Convention, acts under the auspices of UNEP and aims to conserve terrestrial, aquatic, and avian migratory species throughout their range.

questions.question_text: Q5. With reference to ‘LIGO-India’, recently seen in the news, consider the following statements:

It is a collaboration between LIGO Laboratory (USA) and three Indian institutes (IPR, RRCAT, IUCAA).

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:The Act provides for a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj in every state. However, states with a population not exceeding 20 lakhs may not constitute the intermediate level.Statement 2 is not correct:The 'Gram Sabha' is a body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of the Panchayat at the village level, not simply all residents.

questions.question_text: Q2. Which of the following was the primary purpose of the 'Cabinet Mission Plan' of 1946?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To partition India into two sovereign states

options.label: B
options.option_text: To discuss the transfer of power to a united India and set up a Constituent Assembly

options.label: C
options.option_text: To arrest the leaders of the Quit India Movement

options.label: D
options.option_text: To grant Dominion Status to India immediately

questions.explanation: TheCabinet Mission Plan (1946)rejected the demand for a full-fledged Pakistan and instead proposed a loose federation (united India) with a weak centre and strong provinces. Its primary aim was to discuss the transfer of power and set up a Constituent Assembly to frame the Constitution.

questions.question_text: Q3. With reference to the Indian economy, the term 'Capital Account Convertibility' implies:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Freedom to convert rupee into foreign currency for trade in goods and services

options.label: B
options.option_text: Freedom to convert local financial assets into foreign financial assets and vice-versa

options.label: C
options.option_text: The ability of the government to print unlimited currency

options.label: D
options.option_text: Converting the fiscal deficit into capital expenditure

questions.explanation: Capital Account Convertibilityrefers to the freedom to convert local financial assets into foreign financial assets and vice-versa at market-determined rates of exchange. It relates to investment and borrowing (capital flows), unlike Current Account Convertibility which relates to trade in goods and services.

questions.question_text: Q4. Consider the following statements regarding the 'Great Indian Bustard':
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct.The Great Indian Bustard (GIB)  is the state bird of Rajasthan. It is listed as 'Critically Endangered' by the IUCN due to habitat loss and collisions with power lines. It is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, found mainly in Rajasthan and Gujarat.

questions.question_text: Q5. With reference to Lithium-ion batteries, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct:Lithium-ion batteries have a high energy density, allowing them to store more energy in a smaller space.Statement 2 is correct:They do not suffer from the 'memory effect' (a phenomenon where batteries gradually lose their maximum energy capacity if they are repeatedly recharged after being only partially discharged), which was a common issue with Nickel-Cadmium batteries.

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the Irwin Declaration (1929), consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Explanation:In 1929, Viceroy Irwin had vaguely announced that India would be granted dominion status in the future. Known as the Irwin Declaration, it was warmly welcomed by Indians but faced massive backlash back in Britain.The British population was still pro-Empire and India was seen as the Empire’s Crown Jewel. Importantly, as the world economy went into a recession, India was arguably Britain’s most valuable colony with its vast land, resources, and population crucial for its economy.Thus, under pressure from back home, Irwin went back on his word. In a meeting with Gandhi, Muslim League’s Muhhammad Ali Jinnah and a few other leaders, he said that he could not promise India dominion status any time soon.This would be a turning point as the Congress grew increasingly united on the issue. With the British unable to follow through on even reasonable reforms, Indians supported increasingly “radical” goals – a fully independent republic being one of the first.

questions.question_text: Q2. With reference to the Bactrian camels, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Relevance:This question tests knowledge of unique animal adaptations and regional breeds of India. It also helps in distinguishing between desert, cold-desert, and coastal ecosystem species.Explanation:At the annual Republic Day parades, the Indian Army’s Remount and Veterinary Corps (RVC) are generally represented by the dog squad. This year, in a first time, other animals will also be part of the parade.Bactrian camels:Leading the contingent will be Bactrian camels, inducted for animal transport in the cold deserts of Ladakh. Adapted to extreme cold and altitudes above 15,000 feet, these camels can carry loads of up to 250 kilograms and negotiate steep gradients and sandy terrain, supporting logistics and mounted patrolling along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).These ponies carry loads of 40 to 60 kilograms over long distances and are employed for logistics and patrol duties in high Himalayan regions, including Siachen.Hence, statement 4 is correct.The double-humped camel, or Bactrian camel, is found exclusively in the high-altitude cold desert of Ladakh.Hence, statement 1 is correct.Bactrian camels are native to Central Asia, such as Mongolia, China, Kazakhstan, etc.Hence, statement 2 is not correct.Bactrian camels can swim, but they do not naturally swim long distances nor feed on mangroves. These are the traits of Kharai camels.Hence, statement 3 is not correct.

questions.question_text: Q3. The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for solar PV modules covers:
questions.explanation: Relevance:UPSC often tests value-chain based schemes, especially those linked to Atmanirbhar Bharat, clean energy transition, and import substitution.Explanation:The Ministry of Finance and Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) are in discussions to bring out a new capital subsidy scheme for the upstream segment of solar photovoltaic (PV) manufacturing.The existing Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for solar PV modules covers bothupstream— ingot, wafer and polysilicon — anddownstream— solar cell and module manufacturing — segments.However, progress under the PLI scheme has been slower in upstream segments such as polysilicon refining and ingot and wafer production. Polysilicon is a highly electricity-intensive industry. The refining from silica to polysilicon is extremely electricity intensive.

questions.question_text: Q4. With reference to the Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) safety technology, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Relevance:This question tests awareness of emerging transport technologies and intelligent transportation systems (ITS).Explanation:The government is planning to launch Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) safety technology to prevent road accident deaths and reduce traffic.V2V or vehicle-to-vehicle communication is a wireless technology that will enable the vehicles to communicate or talk with one another to share real-time information like speed, location, acceleration, braking, etc. It is the sub-category of Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) and comes under the umbrella of the Intelligent Transport System.Hence, statement 1 is correct.Usually, V2V systems have a range of 300 metres and can detect vehicles in this range. For instance, if a car applies brakes suddenly, the nearby vehicles will get an alert to slow down before seeing it. This will help in reducing crashes.Hence, statement 2 is correct.

questions.question_text: Q5. With reference to the Padma Awards, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Explanation:The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honours of India announced annually on the eve of Republic Day.Hence, statement 1 is correct.The Padma Awards are conferred on the recommendations made by thePadma Awards Committee, which is constituted by the Prime Minister every year. The nomination process is open to the public.Hence, statement 2 is not correct.Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of the country. The number of Bharat Ratna Awards is restricted to a maximum ofthreein a particular year.Hence, statement 4 is not correct.Padma Awards, which were instituted in the year 1954, are announced every year on the occasion of Republic Day except for brief interruption(s) during the years 1978 and 1979 and 1993 to 1997.Hence, statement 3 is correct.Thus, only statements 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.question_text: Q1. Consider the following passage:“In December 1930, the three freedom fighters entered the Writers’ Building of Calcutta, which housed the Secretariat, and shot dead Lt Col N.S. Simpson, the British Inspector General of Prisons, who was known for subjecting Indian prisoners to brutal torture in custody. Following the commotion, one of them consumed potassium cyanide, while other two shot themselves to avoid capture.”The three freedom fighters referred in the passage above are:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Surya Sen, Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal

options.label: B
options.option_text: Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Shyamji Krishna Varma, Pritilata Waddedar

options.label: C
options.option_text: Hemchandra Kanungo, Ullaskar Dutta, Bagha Jatin

options.label: D
options.option_text: Benoy Basu, Badal Gupta and Dinesh Gupta

questions.explanation: Explanation:West Bengal tableau “Swatantrata ka Mantra – Vande Mataram,” celebrated 150 years of the song, honours Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay on Republic Day 2026. It also highlighted many revolutionaries including the trios,Benoy Basu, Badal Gupta and Dinesh Gupta.Set up after 1947 on the opposite side of the wide road in front of Writers’ Building in central Calcutta, the statues of Benoy Basu, Badal Gupta and Dinesh Gupta commemorate the sacrifice of the three men for the freedom of India.In December 1930, the three entered the Writers’ Building, which housed the Secretariat, and shot dead Lt Col N.S. Simpson, the British Inspector General of Prisons, who was known for subjecting Indian prisoners to brutal torture in custody. Following the commotion, Badal Gupta consumed potassium cyanide, while Benoy Basu and Dinesh Gupta shot themselves to avoid capture. Basu was hospitalised but he died days later, while Dinesh Gupta survived the bullet injury, and was arrested, convicted and sentenced to death.Originally named Dalhousie Square, post Independence, the area was renamedB.B.D. Bagh, after the initials of the revolutionaries’ names and a plaque was set up inside Writers’ Building in remembrance.

questions.question_text: Q2. With reference to the volcanoes, consider the following pairs:
questions.explanation: Relevance:This question tests world physical geography and map-based location awareness, specifically regarding global volcanic belts like the Pacific Ring of Fire.Explanation:Mount Vesuvius, Italy:It last erupted in 1944 and is considered one of the most dangerous volcanoes in the world due to the dense population living nearby (Naples area).Hence, pair 1 is correctly marked.Mount Merapi, Indonesia:It is located in Central Java and is one of Indonesia’s most active volcanoes. It erupts frequently, yet villages continue to exist on its slopes due to fertile soil.Hence, pair 2 is not correctly marked.Kilauea, Hawaii, USA:Kilauea is among the world’s most active volcanoes and has been erupting intermittently for decades.Hence, pair 3 is not correctly marked.

questions.question_text: Q3. Which of the following are functions of the central counterparties (CCPs)?
questions.explanation: Relevance:CCPs are crucial financial market infrastructures that interpose themselves between buyers and sellers to ensure smooth clearing and settlement of trades. They are in focus due to rising concerns over financial stability and the recent RBI-ESMA MoU.Explanation:Central counterparties perform two main functions as the intermediary in a market transaction —clearing and settlement— andguarantee the terms of a trade.Hence, statements 1 and 2 are correct.CCPs do not eliminate market or price risk; they only manage counterparty default risk.Hence, statement 3 is not correct.Supervision and regulation are functions of market regulators (e.g., SEBI), not the CCPs themselves.Hence, statement 4 is not correct.

questions.question_text: Q4. With reference to the DRDO’s Long Range Anti-Ship Hypersonic Missile (LR-AShM), consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Relevance:This question tests awareness of India’s latest defence and missile developments by DRDO, especially in hypersonic technology.Explanation:The missile system is designed to meet the coastal battery requirements of the Indian Navy. The LR-AShM is capable of engaging static and moving targets and is designed to carry various payloads to a range of around1,500 kilometers.Hence, statement 3 is not correct.This missile follows aquasi-ballistic trajectorywith hypersonic speeds starting at Mach 10 and maintaining average Mach 5 with multiple skips. Quasi-ballistic missiles begin ballistically but fly lower and manoeuvre in flight to change course and evade interception.Hence, statement 1 is correct.The LR-AShM is configured with atwo-stagesolid propulsion rocket motor system.Hence, statement 2 is not correct.

questions.question_text: Q5. With reference to the Census in India, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Explanation:People opting for the self-enumeration facility in Census 2027—where they fill, complete and submit the document themselves—will be able to do so in 16 languages.The Census has been conducted in India since1872(under Lord Mayo, though the first complete census was in 1881).Census 2027 will be the 16th census overall and the eighth since Independence.The first phase of Census 2027, the Houselisting and Housing Census, is scheduled to begin on April 1 this year. The second phase of the Census, population enumeration, will take place in February 2027.Hence, statements 1 and 2 are correct.

questions.question_text: Q1. Consider the following statements with reference to the Nehru Report of 1928:
questions.explanation: Explanation:In response to the Simon Commission, the INC appointed its own commission underMotilal Nehru(not Jawaharlal Nehru). The Nehru Report demanded that India be granted dominion status within the Empire.Hence, statement 1 is not correct.In the Balfour Declaration of 1926, dominions were defined as "autonomous communities within the British Empire". In 1926, countries like Canada, Australia and New Zealand were granted dominion status.Hence, statement 3 is correct.Crucially, even within the Congress, the Nehru Report did not enjoy universal support. Young leaders such as Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru, Motilal’s own son, wanted India to break all ties with the British Empire. They argued that under dominion status, the British Parliament would still meddle in Indian affairs.Hence, statement 2 is correct.

questions.question_text: Q2. The Indian stretch of the legendary Silk Route once connected Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh to Tibet, China, and Central Asia, passes through:
questions.explanation: Relevance:This question tests map-based knowledge of Himalayan passes and ancient trade routes. It evaluates understanding of India’s historical connectivity with Central Asia, Tibet, and China.Explanation:Before highways, railways, and shipping lanes, India was covered by ancient trade routes. The Indian stretch of the legendary Silk Route once connected Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh to Tibet, China, and Central Asia. Traders moved silk, wool, spices, horses, and turquoise across high-altitude passes such asZoji LaandBaralacha La.The Silk Route passes through:Karakoram Pass, Zoji La, Baralacha La, Chang La, Khardung La, Imis La, Lanakh La, Shipki La, Lipu Lekh, Niti Pass, Mana Pass, etc.Pir Panjal Passis an internal pass connecting Jammu and Kashmir, while theJelep Laconnects Sikkim and Tibet.

questions.question_text: Q3. Consider the following statements regarding India's energy imports:
questions.explanation: Relevance:India–UAE energy cooperation is in focus due to rising crude oil imports and gas security concerns. Data on India’s energy import dependence is frequently tested.Explanation:The UAE is India’sfourth-largestsource of oil imports, behind Russia, Iraq, and Saudi Arabia.Hence, statement 1 is not correct.India depends on imports to meet over 88% of its oil demand and around half of its natural gas demand. questions.question_text: Q4. The ‘Haven-1’ refers to:

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.option_text: reusable hypersonic spaceplane developed for orbital tourism

options.label: C

questions.question_text: Q5. Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Constitution:

questions.question_text: Q1. Why was January 26 chosen as India’s Republic Day?

options.label: A
options.option_text: On this day in 1950, the Constituent Assembly completed the drafting of the Constitution

options.label: B
options.option_text: On this day in 1930, the Indian National Congress declared Purna Swaraj

options.label: C
options.option_text: On this day in 1947, the Indian Independence Act came into force

options.label: D
options.option_text: On this day in 1949, the Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly

questions.explanation: Explanation:Since 1950, January 26 has marked the day India’s Constitution came into effect. However, the Constitution was prepared way before the chosen date, adopted officially by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949.On January 26, 1930, the historic “Poorna Swaraj” declaration was officially promulgated, beginning the final phase of India’s freedom struggle where the goal would be complete independence from British rule.Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Q2. With reference to the polar vortex, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Relevance:This question tests conceptual clarity in dynamic climatology, especially vertical atmospheric structure (troposphere vs stratosphere). It assesses understanding of polar vortex–jet stream interaction and extreme weather mechanisms.Explanation:The polar vortex is a large area of low-pressure and cold air that swirls like a wheel around both of the Earth’s polar regions. There are two types of polar vortex: tropospheric and stratospheric.The tropospheric polar vortex occurs at the lowest layer of the atmosphere — it extends from the surface up to about 10 km to 15 km — where most weather phenomena occur.The stratospheric polar vortex occurs at around 15 km to 50 km high. Unlike the tropospheric polar vortex, thestratospheric polar vortex disappears during the summer and is the strongest during the autumn. Hence, statement 2 is not correct.Thetropospheric polar vortex is associated with the Polar jet streamwhile the stratospheric polar vortex is associated with the Polar night jet. Hence, statement 1 is not correct.

According to Sarangi, this is a structural challenge linked to the faster execution timelines of renewable projects.Evacuation of RE power is a major challenge because renewable power plants can become operational much faster than conventional thermal power plants.Hence, statements 1 and 2 are correct.A coal-based power plant typically takes five to six years to become operational. So, the transmission system used to get ready by that time. But now, a solar power plant is coming up within one to two years. A wind turbine is getting ready within a one-year period, whereas the transmission system is still taking three to four to five years.Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct and Statement 2 is the correct explanation for Statement 1.

questions.question_text: Q4. With reference to hypoxia and hypothermia, consider the following statements:

It is also important for distinguishing between hypoxia, hypothermia, and hyperthermia, a common UPSC trap area.Explanation:Hypoxiais caused by inadequate oxygen, while hypothermia is afall in core body temperatureto a level where normal physical and brain functions are impaired. questions.question_text: Q5. Consider the following statements regarding Article 20:
questions.explanation: Relevance:This question tests understanding of Article 20 and constitutional protections in criminal jurisprudence. It checks clarity on double jeopardy and protection against self-incrimination.Explanation:Article 20 of the Constitution of India provides for the protection in respect of conviction for offences.No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the Act charged as an offence, nor be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence.No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.Hence, statement 1 is not correct.No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.Hence, statement 2 is not correct.

questions.question_text: Q3. With reference to the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Relevance:JJM is a flagship scheme, frequently in news for coverage milestones, reforms in funding, and digital monitoring, making it a high-probability area for UPSC Prelims 2026.Explanation:Jal Jeevan Mission is envisioned to provide safe and adequate drinking water through individual household tap connections by 2024 to all households in rural India.Hence, statement 1 is correct.The Jal Jeevan Mission will be based on a community approach to water and will include extensive Information, Education and communication as a key component of the mission.Hence, statement 2 is correct.States would receive funds under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) only after signing of separate MoUs, with each scheme mapped through a unique Scheme ID and future releases linked to the demonstration of 15 days of continuous water supply.Hence, statement 3 is correct.Therefore, all three statements are correct.

questions.question_text: Q4. Consider the following statements about GPS interference:
questions.explanation: Relevance:This question tests understanding of electronic warfare, satellite navigation systems, and signal interference techniques. It is important for questions related to cyber security, defence technology, and strategic communications.Explanation:GPS jamming, also known as GPS intervention, occurs when a device (jammer) emitsstrongradio signals (not weaker) on GPS frequencies in order to overcome weaker signals. This impairs the operation of GPS systems by preventing receivers from determining location or time.Hence, statement 1 is not correct.GPS spoofing occurs when a device transmits signals on thesamefrequencies (not different) utilised by GPS satellites, overpowering or blocking GPS receivers from acquiring or sustaining the correct satellite signals. Unlike jamming, which completely interrupts transmissions, spoofing tricks the receiver into believing fake data.Hence, statement 2 is not correct.

questions.question_text: Q5. The provision of ‘Abolition of Untouchability’ is provided in the:
questions.explanation: Relevance:This question tests factual knowledge of Fundamental Rights and their specific constitutional articles. It is important for mapping social justice provisions to exact articles of the Constitution.Explanation:Article 17of the Constitution of India provides for the Abolition of Untouchability. The "Untouchability" is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. The enforcement of any disability arising out of "Untouchability" shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.Article 15 deals with Prohibition of discrimination.Article 16 deals with Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.Article 18 deals with Abolition of titles.

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the Chagos Islands, consider the following statements:

questions.question_text: Q3. With reference to the Light Water Reactors (LWRs), consider the following statements:

questions.question_text: Q4. With reference to the Artemis II, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Relevance:UPSC asks such questions to test whether candidates track major global science–technology developments.Explanation:The Artemis II test flight will be NASA’s first mission with crew aboard the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and Orion spacecraft.Hence, statement 1 is correct.The crew will travel around the Moon before returning to Earth to test systems needed for future landings.Hence, statement 2 is correct.NASA has invited the public to send their names to the Moon before (e.g., Artemis I, Mars missions).Hence, statement 3 is not correct.

questions.question_text: Q5. The special address by the Governor is given at:
questions.explanation: Relevance:The Governor’s Special Address under Article 176 tests understanding of when constitutional mandates apply.Explanation:Article 176 states the Governor shall address the Legislative Assembly at thecommencement of the first session after each general electionand at thecommencement of the first session of each year.The Governor doesnotaddress every session (e.g., Monsoon or Winter sessions, unless they are the first of the year).Hence, statements 1 and 2 are correct, and 3 is not correct.

questions.question_text: Q1. Recently, the United States withdrew from over 60 major international organisations and agreements. Which of the following international organisations is the United States STILL a part of?

questions.question_text: Q2. The Polavaram Irrigation Project was recently in the news. It is constructed across the:

questions.question_text: Q3. With reference to crude oil, consider the following statements:

questions.question_text: Q4. With reference to solar storms, consider the following statements:

questions.explanation: Relevance:Tests understanding of who performs which election-related function.Explanation:BLOs are grassroots functionaries responsible for:1. questions.question_text: Q3. With reference to the Indian rupee, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Relevance:Tests understanding of exchange rate determinants, BoP, and global linkages of the Indian rupee.Explanation:A strong balance of payments position helps the currency remain stable.Hence, statement 1 is correct.External factors, such as the US dollar's performance (DXY index) and global oil prices, significantly affect the rupee's value.Hence, statement 2 is not correct.Depreciation doesnot alwaysimprove the trade balance immediately (due to the J-curve effect and inelastic demand for essential imports like oil).Hence, statement 3 is not correct.

questions.question_text: Q5. As per Article 39 of the Constitution of India, the State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing —
questions.explanation: Relevance:Article 39 is a high-yield DPSP provision, frequently tested to distinguish it from Fundamental Rights.Explanation:Article 39(a) secures the right to an adequate means of livelihood for men and women equally.Hence, statement 1 is correct.Article 39(b) ensures material resources are distributed to subserve the common good.Hence, statement 3 is correct.Free and compulsory education is covered underArticle 21A(Fundamental Right) and Article 45, not Article 39.Hence, statement 2 is not correct.

questions.question_text: Q1. With reference to the Genocide Convention, consider the following statements:
questions.explanation: Relevance:This question links current international conflicts with legal accountability frameworks under the Genocide Convention.Explanation:The Genocide Convention was adopted by the UN after World War II to prevent and punish the crime of genocide.Hence, statement 1 is correct.The Convention imposeserga omnesobligations (obligations towards the international community as a whole). questions.question_text: Q2. Which of the following factors can contribute to the ecological degradation of forests?

questions.question_text: Q1. Which of the following countries are members of the Mercosur (South American trade bloc)?
